note: A new procurement watch briefed from the example: both questions answered by tile, one change (checked as orders are placed), armed.

journey.title: Procurement spend 2.5% lower: check every new order against the frameworks
journey.prompt: Help me take 2.5% off procurement spend across all our capital projects. Check every new order line against the framework agreements and benchmark prices, tell me when something goes off-framework or above benchmark, and work out what can still be done before I ask.

reads.res: Frameworks are mandatory above $25k per line where one covers the item · a saving counts once it is in an order or a signed contract
Target 2.5% of $968.0M addressable capital spend: $24.2M by 30 June 2027
Every order line with its item, supplier and unit price · 4 frameworks, 9 priced items · category benchmarks
New order lines load nightly at 02:00. Next: tonight, Tuesday 20 October, with Monday’s orders
“Belmara rate base” reads the same awards for its prudence check; I read it whenever this fires
No distribution list is connected; I need to know who to tell
Savings tracker: $8.7M secured · off-framework buying about $1.4M above framework since April · the catalogue still defaults to the spot suppliers

questions.title: What should count as a breach?
questions.text: Four frameworks cover pipe, fittings, valves, hydrants, meters and GAC media. Items no framework covers can still be checked against the category benchmark, which fires more often.

tiles.t: Any line above $25k off a framework that covers it
Also any line more than 5% above the category benchmark
A digest of every load, flagged or not

questions.title: Who is told when it fires?
questions.text: No project-manager list is connected. The note goes out without waiting for you, so pick who should see it.

tiles.t: Me, the project managers and Procurement
tiles.s: Everyone who can change an order

over.where: In our data, on every order as it is placed, not only at the nightly load. A line caught before the supplier confirms it can still be changed at no cost.

history.what: Checked on every order as it is placed

nodes.title: Confirm what the order load flagged, and size it
nodes.purpose: Which lines are off-framework or above benchmark, and by how much.
nodes.how: Every new order line against the framework price schedules and the category benchmarks: the unit price paid, the framework price, the premium, and whether the supplier has confirmed the line. Limited to the lines in the load that fired the rule.
nodes.check: Every flagged line recomputes from its quantity, unit price and framework price.

nodes.title: Why it happened, and whether anyone raised it
nodes.purpose: Is this new, and is someone already on it.
nodes.how: Off-framework buying by category since April, the framework lead times, the ordering catalogue, and what Procurement and the project managers have said.
draws: Outlook: Procurement and project managers (S1, S2, S3)
nodes.check: Every figure since April recomputes from the order lines.

nodes.title: Trace each line against its framework price
nodes.purpose: The premium item by item, and whether the policy allowed it.
nodes.how: For each flagged line: the framework that covers the item, its price, the premium, and the Procurement exception the policy requires on the order.
nodes.check: The line premiums sum to the batch premium.

nodes.title: What can still be done, including nothing
nodes.purpose: Each course of action with the saving it keeps, checked against open goals.
nodes.how: Each option with the saving it keeps against the 2.5% target, what it costs (restocking, delay), who has to agree, and an honest statement if nothing can be recovered; read the open goals on this role.
nodes.check: Every option states the saving it keeps and what it costs.

nodes.title: Note to the people you chose
nodes.purpose: One page, sent without waiting for you.
nodes.how: The lines, why they went off-framework, the premium, the options, and the catalogue fix; on the off-framework order note template.
nodes.check: Every figure in the note links back to its step.
